rationale: B wins because its best material knows what a reporter will kill: “The $550 claim: what a flight-deal subscription actually saves, and how it's counted” is a real data/service angle with a kill condition. A spends one slot on “The company once known as Scott's Cheap Flights just built an AI travel app,” which is an underfed corporate biography trying to pass as news. But B nearly face-plants with “a $200 mistake fare into a booked week,” a fake number and booking implication the update does not support, so this is a slight win, not a parade.
gaps_in_A: “Expedia, Kayak, and Hopper have bolted AI planners onto their products” is outside the supplied update; maybe true, but in this exercise it is an unsupported competitive claim doing load-bearing work.

“The company once known as Scott's Cheap Flights just built an AI travel app” overstates a planner launch into a company-evolution story without the rebrand timeline, product roadmap, or executive argument needed to make that arc real.
“A tech reporter or columnist” is too mushy for the contrarian AI-agent angle; the rest of the line narrows it, but the beat starts with a delete-trigger generality.

“newsletter-first companies convert free audiences” smuggles in company-history framing the update does not provide. Formerly Scott's Cheap Flights is a fact; newsletter-to-platform thesis is not yet earned.
gaps_in_B: “turns a $200 mistake fare into a booked week” invents the $200 fare and implies booking, while the update explicitly says no airline or hotel booking happens in-app.
“the free tier finds the fare, the paid tier tells you what to do with it” overstates the tier mechanics. We know the planner is Premium-only; we do not know the free tier gets that same alert flow.
“Story type: funding-mechanics” is the wrong label. There is no funding story here; this is freemium conversion/paywall strategy.

“Next step: newsjack-detector” is a sideways move for a launch package. The immediate next step is demo access, $550 methodology, paid-member count, and an on-record spokesperson. Hunt a live peg after the core proof is clean.
